CELEBRATING DIFFERENCE, NURTURING POTENTIAL.
Our students
We offer an education to a community of neurodiverse learners, most of whom are autistic, with many also experiencing co-occurring conditions such as dyslexia, dyspraxia (DCD), dyscalculia and ADHD. Our students range from Year 4 to Year 13.
Many of our young people have found it difficult to engage with traditional teaching methods or have faced barriers caused by specific learning differences. Large schools and classrooms can often feel overwhelming, and high levels of anxiety are common — which is why our students flourish in an environment where they feel safe, understood, and supported through trusting relationships with staff.
Our provision is structured into a Middle School, Upper School, and Sixth Form, offering the full range of curriculum subjects and opportunities to achieve GCSE and A-level qualifications.
It is a pleasure to welcome you to our warm and caring community.
Here, we celebrate individuality, nurture each student’s unique strengths, and spark a curiosity that lasts a lifetime. Every child is valued for who they are and supported to discover who they can become. We believe learning happens best when students feel safe, understood, and surrounded by people who believe in them. Our school is a place where it’s okay to take risks, make mistakes, and try again — where challenges are met with encouragement and successes are celebrated, no matter how small.
We offer a rich academic education through a specialist approach, set within a supportive and collaborative school community. By breaking down the barriers and limits too often placed on students. We inspire a genuine love of learning, where creativity and individuality are celebrated.
Our skilled and caring team of educators, therapists, and support staff work in harmony to provide a fully integrated, whole-school approach. Together, we nurture each child’s academic and social growth while supporting their overall well-being.
“Woodstock House has been such a turning point for our daughter. She arrived so anxious and unsure of herself, and leaves confident and happy. Thanks to you and the team for the incredible work you do.”

We are delighted to publish our external exam results for the academic year, 2023-24. Congratulations to our students and staff for all that they have achieved.

2022
We are extremely pleased to announce their external exam results for the academic year, 2022-23 including our January and May/June examinations, and would like to congratulate all our students and staff for their efforts and achievements over this academic year. We are very proud of everyone’s effort and outcomes this year and whilst we realise that life is much more than exam results, we also want to celebrate the progress and outcomes of our students.
2021
We are very proud to say that for the fifth consecutive year, students graduating from year 11 have at least 6 GCSEs with grade 5 and above. We are also proud that in 2021, all our year 10 students achieved 6 GCSEs at level 4 and above and now move on to further GCSE studies.
Our A-Level students surpassed themselves this year and our graduating year 13 student received 3 A-star grades in Maths, Further Maths and Economics and is off to study MORSE at Warwick University. We are also proud of another lower 6th student who gained a complete A-Level Maths at grade A-star in only one year.

Our vision is to celebrate our students’ unique qualities and encourage individuality.
We learn from each other. We are curious, we are compassionate. We nurture each student’s potential. We give our students the courage to question, to develop their curiosity, to push through barriers, to be proud of who they are and where they are going. We strive to ensure that each student that leaves us has had the best possible opportunities, that they know they will always be good enough. We are more than a learning environment; we are a community. To achieve this, we provide a safe and inclusive setting that allows each learner the opportunity to access education that meets their individual needs.
Our ethos
Our community is vibrant and creative, underpinned by a shared sense of belonging and purpose. We believe that learning is a joy when it is driven by internal motivation and that we need to provide an environment which encourages curiosity, one where it is safe to take chances and make mistakes. This approach will encourage students to be engaged with their learning and the world around them.
We are curious about our students, about what motivates, interests and regulates them and this understanding underpins our relationships. We are adaptable and use a range of methods and resources to encourage reciprocal interactions and facilitate learning.
Our values
COMMUNITY
We foster a strong sense of belonging and shared purpose, creating a supportive community where everyone if valued.
COLLABORATION
Our staff work in partnership with our students to support them in achieving their learning goals, and to create an environment and community that we are all happy and content to be part of.
CURIOSITY
Curiosity thrives where there is trust. We are curious to understand who our students are, how they learn and what inspires them. We wish to foster curiosity in our students about the world around them. We want our students to feel safe enough to ponder and to question.
COMPASSION
We understand our students emotional, social and academic individual needs and work to build trust and strong relationships
It’s all in the logo…
Our logo reflects all four of our values and truly embodies the nurturing spirit of our staff. It represents how we support every student to grow, thrive, and flourish.

A safe space
Our school is committed to ensuring every child feels supported and secure. When a student is experiencing worry or upset, staff are on hand to provide calm and caring guidance. Depending on the situation, this may include offering a quiet moment in a sensory-friendly environment, time with a trusted adult, or opportunities to practise strategies that help them self-regulate. We prioritise emotional wellbeing, ensuring that no student is ever left to manage difficult feelings alone.
Lunch
All students bring a packed lunch to school. We know that many of our students have food preferences and sensory sensitivities, and we understand that this can impact what they eat. Some students have allergies so please don’t bring nuts into school.
Mobile Phones
We are a mobile phone free school. We understand that many of our students travel long distances to come to school and use their devices for regulation and music therefore, if students do bring devices to school, we ask for them to be switched off and handed it upon arrival at school. Devices are kept safe and returned to students at the end of the school day.

Uniform
At Woodstock House, we believe that wearing a uniform can foster a sense of belonging and equality between students. However, we also recognise that many of our students have sensory differences that can make wearing particular clothes difficult and our priority is that students feel comfortable and appropriately dressed for school. To support this, we have uniform guidelines, outlined below. Should further adaptations be necessary, please discuss this with the relevant member of staff.
Years 4-11
Please send students in clothing they will be comfortable and happy in that follow the below:• A polo / or T-shirt in Cadbury purple• Black sweatshirt / jumper• Black trousers / shorts or knee-length skirt• Black shoes / trainers PE kits to follow suit as above, students can come into school wearing their PE kits for the day.
Sixth Form
Sixth form pupils can choose to either wear school uniform or smart casual clothing. Smart casual should be suitable for work in a professional environment. The focus is on looking neat and presentable without causing discomfort or anxiety.

Finding the right setting
We recognise that it can be a challenging journey to get the right educational setting for your child. If you are considering Woodstock House, we will support and work closely with you to ensure that the right decisions are made for them.Our process is in 4 main steps:
If you feel that Woodstock House is the right environment for your child, the first step is to email our admissions team at admissions@woodstockhouseschool.co.uk with the following details:– Your full name– Contact details– Child’s full name– EHCPPlease also include any additional information that may be useful, such as details not covered in the EHCP or updates to any outdated information.Once we receive your email, a member of our team will contact you to gain a fuller understanding of your child’s individual needs.
We will invite you as parent(s) to visit our school for a more in-depth discussion and a tour. There will be opportunities for you to ask any questions that you may have. If we feel that we can meet your child’s needs, we will arrange a time for them to visit and tour the school with you.
If all parties feel this could be the right setting for your child, we will organise trial sessions. These allow them to experience our supportive environment, understand our friendly and tailored teaching methods, and become familiar with our school community. These sessions allow us to observe your child’s strengths and interests. This also enables us to assess the support and care that would be required to help them transition and long term, to help them flourish and reach their full potential.
Following the trial sessions, if Woodstock House is the right environment for your child we will offer a place and once accepted will work with you to ensure a successful transition to Woodstock House.
